# Two-mass D0 (OneLOop's boxf2, and boxf5 for opposite masses) with complex masses, where
# OneLOop 3.6 is wrong in double and quadruple precision alike, and so was this crate before
# it took Denner and Dittmaier's sheets for a width (box_integral::two_mass_sheets).
# OneLOop's value is in the comment before each row. Rows: NinjaRS's reproducer, then rows of
# random sweeps that OneLOop and this crate got wrong in the same rows: per mass pattern
# 8 to 18 of 2000 boxes with |Im m^2| from 1e-3 to 0.5 of Re m^2 (by 0.6 to 17 relative to
# the value), 2 to 10 of 500 with one real mass, 3 to 11 of 1000 with the widths divided by
# 1e6, 4 to 10 of 500 next to a collinear limit (an invariant between the massless lines of
# 1e-12 to 1e-3) and to Y02 Y13 = Y01 Y23 (by up to 9e4), and 2 of 200 boxes with a real mass
# on shell (in all 24 relabellings).
# References: Denner and Dittmaier's two-mass box (arXiv:1005.2076, eqs. (3.78)-(3.80): the
# continued dilogarithms with eta terms of the principal logarithms of x_k and of the ratios
# Y23/Y02, Y13/Y01 and r03k; with lines 0 and 3 the massive lines, in each of the four such
# labellings, which agree), in mpmath at 40 digits with the exact binary64 inputs. COLLIER
# 1.2.9 in quadruple precision (its COLI and DD branches, independent of both OneLOop and this
# crate) agrees within the bound in the comment. For the first row a direct Feynman-parameter
# integral (primary sectors, contour deformation, nested tanh-sinh, no closed-form one-loop
# code) gives -7.161258e-4 + 0.08313160864i (h = 0.025, lambda = 0.15: within 2e-8 of the
# reference relative to |D0|; lambda = 0.1 within 2e-6), where OneLOop is 0.95 away.
